sections.overview: The Jack Dempsey is a freshwater cichlid native to the Atlantic slope of Central America.
sections.identification: It is a robust, spotted fish that can reach about 25 centimetres in total length.
sections.habitat: It occurs in warm, slow waters, including marshes, canals and lower river valleys.
sections.diet: It eats animal prey such as worms, crustaceans, insects and fish.
sections.behavior: Outside its native range, it has been recorded as an introduced fish in several places.
sections.reproduction: It lays eggs on a substrate, and both parents guard the eggs and young.
sections.ecology: It is a benthopelagic, non-migratory fish of lowland freshwater habitats.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a global IUCN category of Least Concern, assessed in 2018.
